'''Doron Aurbach''' ({{langx|he|דורון אורבך}}; born 3 September 1952) is an Israeli [[Electrochemistry|electrochemist]], [[Materials science|materials]] and [[Surface science|surface]] scientist.

==Biography==
Doron Aurbach<ref name=BIU>[https://ch.biu.ac.il/aurbach Doron Aurbach, Department of Chemistry, Bar-Ilan University]</ref> was born in 1952 in Israel to parents who survived the [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] and fought the [[1948 Arab–Israeli War]], grew up in [[Ramat Gan]] and studied in [[:he: תיכון בליך|Blich High School]]. He served in [[Golani Brigade|Sayeret Golani]] reconnaissance unit, a.k.a. 631st Reconnaissance Battalion, (an [[Israeli special forces units#Reconnaissance units|Israeli special force unit]]) and fought west to the [[Suez Canal]] during the [[Yom Kippur War]] (1973). Later he returned to [[Golani Brigade#Yom Kippur War|Golani Brigade]] as a deputy commander of a [[combat support company]], and was discharged from [[Reserve duty (Israel)|reserve duty]] with a rank of a [[Major (rank)|Major]] ({{langx|he|רב סרן}}), at the age of 46, as a patrol officer in the [[Armored Corps (Israel)|Armored Corps]].

He is married to Sara, an [[educational counselor]] by training who writes [[Children's literature|children's books]]. They live in [[Bnei Brak]] and have seven children and dozens of grandchildren.

==Academic career==
He obtained his BSc (1977), MSc (1979) and PhD (1983, summa cum laude) from the Chemistry Department at [[Bar-Ilan University]] (BIU). In parallel to his PhD degree, he completed a full degree in [[chemical engineering]] (1981) from the [[Technion]] (Israel Institute of Technology).<ref name=BIU />
He was a postdoctoral fellow (1983-1985) at [[Case Western Reserve University]] (CWRU) [[Cleveland]] Ohio, led by Professor [[Ernest B. Yeager]].

In 1985 he joined the Chemistry Department at Bar-Ilan University and founded the electrochemistry group. Since October 1996 he is a full professor in the Chemistry Department and a [[Academic Senate|Senate member]] at BIU. Between 2001 and 2005 he chaired the Chemistry Department and between 2010 and 2016 he chaired the Israel Labs Accreditation Authority. Aurbach is the Director of the Energy and Sustainable Center of Bar-Ilan University which he founded in 2021.<ref>[https://www.biu.ac.il/en/page/1300 Bar-Ilan’s National Institute for Sustainable Energy]</ref> Aurbach's group belongs (together with other research groups from the US, Canada, Switzerland, Japan, and Germany) to a network of excellence in the field of advanced materials for [[Electric power|power sources]], founded and supported by [[BASF]]. His group benefits from a long-term collaboration with [[General Motors]], working together on advanced power sources for [[electric vehicle|electro-mobility]] (electric vehicles). Aurbach manages a budget of more than 56 million [[Israeli new shekel|NIS]] as a founder and a leader of the Israel National Research Center for [[Electrochemical cell|Electrochemical]] [[Propulsion]] (INREP),<ref>[http://inrep.org.il/members/prof-doron-aurbach/ Israel National Research Center for Electrochemical Propulsion website]</ref> comprising 26 research groups from seven Israeli institutions supported by the [[Council for Higher Education in Israel|Israel Council for Higher Education]] and the Prime-Minister's office. Aurbach is the head of the newly established center for Energy and Sustainability at Bar-Ilan University.<ref>[https://www.biu.ac.il/en/page/1300 Bar Ilan Center for Energy and Sustainability]</ref>

Aurbach is a member of the small management team called IMLB LLC Ltd of the world organization of the advanced [[Lithium-ion battery|Li batteries]] community. Aurbach belongs to the international scientific board of the French Energy Network RS2E<ref>[https://www.energie-rs2e.com/en RS2E French research network on electromechanical energy storage]</ref> and to the international scientific board of [[Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology|Daegu Institute of Technology]] (DGIST) in [[South Korea]].

He is a Fellow of the [[Electrochemical Society]] (ECS),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Doron Aurbach |url=https://www.electrochem.org/aurbach |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=ECS |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Materials Research Society]] (MRS), the [[International Society of Electrochemistry]] (ISE), and a member in the European Academy of Science (since 2015). Aurbach serves (since 2003) as an Editor for the [[Journal of the Electrochemical Society]]. During 2007 and 2015 he served also as a Senior Editor for the Journal of [[Solid-state chemistry|Solid-State]] Electrochemistry ([[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]).<ref>[https://link.springer.com/journal/10008 Journal of Solid-State Electrochemistry (Springer)]</ref>
Among his students are Prof. [[:he:אריה צבן|Arie Zaban]], President of Bar-Ilan University, Prof. Yair Ein-Eli,<ref>[https://materials.technion.ac.il/about/message-from-the-dean/ Dean of Materials Science and Engineering - Technion]</ref> Dean of the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology#Materials Science and Engineering|faculty of Materials Science and Engineering]] at the Technion, and a number of other senior academic faculty members.

==Awards==
Doron Aurbach has won several prizes, among them is the 2020 Israel Chemical Society (ICS) Gold Medal,<ref name=ICS2020>[https://www.chemistry.org.il/ics-medal The 2020 ICS Gold Medal]</ref> the Eric and Sheila Samsom Prime Minister's Prize for Innovation in [[alternative fuel]]s for Transportation (2018).<ref name=Samsom>[http://www.fuelchoicessummit.com/Award.aspx The 2018 Samsom Prime Minister's Prize for Innovation in alternative fuels for Transportation]</ref><ref>[https://embassies.gov.il/UnGeneva/NewsAndEvents/Pages/PM-Netanyahu-attends-6th-annual-Smart-Mobility-Summit-30-Oct-2018.aspx Mission of Israel to the UN in Geneva]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20181029015608/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-10/29/c_137564841.htm Israeli, Finnish scientists win 1 mln USD for innovation in alternative fuels - Xinhua news]</ref> His other awards include the [[Alexander Frumkin]] Medal of the [[International Society of Electrochemistry]]<ref name=Frumkin>[https://www.ise-online.org/awards/frumkin.php Frumkin Memorial Medal - ISE]</ref> (2018), [[Allen J. Bard]] Medal of the [[Electrochemical Society]]<ref name=Brad>[https://www.electrochem.org/bard-award Allen J. Bard Award in Electrochemical Science]</ref> (2017), Ernest B. Yeager award of the International Battery Association (IBA) for career-long achievements in power sources research<ref name= Yeager>[https://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=33&pt=20&pid=4&level=1&cPath=4&type=1&news=2077 Prof. winner of the 2014 Ernest B. Yeager Award, Bar-Ilan Spokesman office]</ref> (2014), the [[Izaak Kolthoff|Kolthoff]] prize of the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]] for excellence in chemical research (2013),<ref>[https://chemistry.technion.ac.il/kolthoff-annual-prize/ Kolthoff annual prize]</ref> the Research Award of the Battery Division of the [[Electrochemical Society]] (2013),<ref name=ECSb>[https://www.electrochem.org/battery-division-research-award ECS - Battery Division Research Award]</ref> the Israel Chemical Society Prize of Excellence (2012),<ref>[https://www.chemistry.org.il/outstanding-scientist The ICS Prize for the Outstanding Scientist]</ref> the Landau Prize for [[Green chemistry|Green Chemistry]] (2011),<ref>[https://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=33&pt=20&pid=33&level=2&cPath=33&type=1&news=1309 Landau Prize Awarded to Three Bar-Ilan University Faculty Members]</ref> the Edwards Company Prize of the Israel Vacuum Society for Research Excellence (2007)<ref>[https://www.ivs.org.il/ IVS - Israel Vacuum Society]</ref> and the Technology Award of the Battery Division of the [[Electrochemical Society]] (2005).<ref name=ECSb />

==Publications==
Aurbach has published more than 750 research papers in leading electrochemistry, materials science, and physical chemistry journals. These papers have been cited < 86200 times with [[h-index]] 143 (Google Scholar).<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=IwxntTAAAAAJ&hl=en Google Scholar - Doron Aurbach]</ref> The statistics from the [[Web of Science]] are h-index 127, < 68000 citations (May 2022). During 2021 alone, he was cited nearly 8400 times ([[Web of Science]]); 9800 (Google Scholar).<ref>[https://www.msesupplies.com/blogs/news/2016-the-most-cited-researchers-in-materials-science-and-engineering-by-elsevier-scopus-data The 2016 List of Most Cited Researchers in Materials Science and Engineering by Elsevier Scopus Data]</ref><ref>[http://www.webometrics.info/en/hlargerthan100 3160 Highly Cited Researchers (h>100) according to their Google Scholar Citations public profiles]</ref> He belongs to the most cited scientists (top 1%) in 2018-2021 as published by the Web of Science and Clarivate analytics. Aurbach is in the list of the world's most influential researchers of the past decade, demonstrated by the production of multiple highly cited papers that rank in the top 1% by citations for field and year in Web of Science.<ref>[https://recognition.webofsciencegroup.com/awards/highly-cited/2019/ Highly Cited Researchers Powered by Web of Science]</ref> According to Research.com, a platform that offers credible data on scientific contributions, Aurbach ranks 89th and 133rd on the list of the world's leading scientists in Chemistry and Material Science, respectively. He ranks 2nd in the list of leading scientists of Israel in both fields.<ref>[https://research.com/scientists-rankings/chemistry Top Chemistry Scientists published by Research.com]</ref>
